History:
• 48-year-old male presenting with acute onset watery diarrhoea for the past 3 days  
• Initial episode began with 2 bouts of vomiting (now resolved) followed immediately by diarrhoea; frequency 5-6 loose, watery stools/day  
• No visible blood in stool, no abdominal pain, no headaches or myalgias  
• Reports feeling dehydrated, weak, poor appetite, limited oral intake; felt mildly febrile on day 1 but afebrile currently  
• No known food triggers, no recent takeaway/restaurant meals, no known sick contacts  
• Lives alone; works as a software engineer; off work last 3 days  

Past Medical History:
• Asthma (intermittent)  
• Medications: Blue inhaler (likely salbutamol) – dose/route/frequency not documented  
• Drug allergies: None known  
• Family history: Father – hypertension, deceased from bowel cancer at age ~?; Mother – type 2 diabetes  
• Social: Non-smoker, infrequent social alcohol use  

Physical Examination:
(telemedicine – limited)  
• Appearance: patient reports weakness but was able to converse appropriately  
• No reported abdominal tenderness or swelling  
• No reported fever at time of consult  
• No haematemesis or haematochezia  

Impression:
Acute gastroenteritis (likely viral) with dehydration risk  

Management Plan:
• Encourage liberal oral fluids; advise oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) as available over the counter  
• Paracetamol for fever or malaise (dose not documented)  
• Rest and remain off work; may return after 24–48 h symptom-free  
• Monitor hydration status (urine output, dizziness); seek urgent care if inability to keep fluids down, bloody stools, high fever, or worsening symptoms  
• Follow-up: re-assessment if not improved within one week or sooner if red-flag symptoms occur  

Patient Summary:
Mr. Robert, 48, likely has viral gastroenteritis causing 3 days of watery diarrhoea and prior brief vomiting. No alarming features identified. Management is conservative with hydration, oral rehydration salts, and symptomatic relief; instructed to follow up if not improving.  

Key Takeaways:
• Drink plenty of clear fluids and use Dioralyte to replace lost salts.  
• Take paracetamol as needed for fever or discomfort.  
• Stay off work until you have been diarrhoea-free for at least 24–48 hours.  

Next Steps:
• Self-monitor over the next few days; if diarrhoea persists beyond 5–7 days, or red-flag symptoms develop, schedule an in-person review  
• Consider stool culture or blood tests if symptoms fail to resolve or if there is blood in stool
